(sec-item-objectconnectoruser)=
# ObjectConnectorUser

A connector of two markers whose forces are a user function of the frames and twists of the markers - their positions, rotations, velocities and angular velocities -: it returns the forces and torques on the markers, which the connector applies through the marker Jacobians - a spring-damper, a bushing, a contact of two points -, also as symbolic user function. For forces at points of a body that the function computes itself, as a contact searching the closest point on a flexible body, a second user function reads any number of markers of any type and applies forces through them. A NodeGenericData keeps a state, which a postNewtonStepUserFunction updates, as for contact or friction; its Jacobian is computed numerically.

## Interface

- Nodes it takes: [](#sec-item-nodegenericdata)

## Parameters

The parameters of the item; in a dictionary, its type is 'ConnectorUser':

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **name** | String |  | '' | connector's unique name |
| **markerNumbers** | ArrayMarkerIndex |  | [] | (symbol: $[m_0,\,m_1,\,\ldots]\tp$) the markers: two Position markers for the forceUserFunction; at least one of any type for the markerAccessUserFunction; the user functions get them in this order |
| **requestedMarkerType** | MarkerType |  | MarkerType._None | the types every marker must provide, checked at Assemble, e.g. exu.MarkerType.Position, or exu.MarkerType.Position \| exu.MarkerType.Orientation for torques; exu.MarkerType._None: markers of any type (#3105) |
| **nodeNumber** | NodeIndex |  | invalid (-1) | (symbol: $n_d$) node number of a NodeGenericData, whose data coordinates the user functions get, e.g. the state of a contact; optional, needed for a postNewtonStepUserFunction (#3102) |
| **parameters** | NumpyVector |  | [] | (symbol: $\pv_{par} \in \Rcal^{n_p}$) the parameters of the connector, of any length, passed to the user function; see exudyn.advancedUtilities.ParameterLayout |
| **activeConnector** | Bool |  | True | flag, which determines, if the connector is active; used to deactivate (temporarily) a connector |
| **forceUserFunction** | ObjectConnectorUserForceUserFunction |  | 0 | A Python or symbolic user function which returns the forces (and torques) on the two markers from their states (#3119); without it and without markerAccessUserFunction, the connector applies no forces |
| **markerAccessUserFunction** | ObjectConnectorUserMarkerAccessUserFunction |  | 0 | A Python user function which reads the markers and applies forces through them, also at points of their bodies it computes, e.g. for a contact on a flexible body; instead of forceUserFunction, not recordable (#2975) |
| **postNewtonStepUserFunction** | ObjectConnectorUserPostNewtonStepUserFunction |  | 0 | A Python user function which updates the data coordinates of the data node after each Newton iteration and returns them with the error of the switch, for contact, friction and other discontinuous states; needs nodeNumber (#3102) |
| **visualization** | VObjectConnectorUser |  |  | parameters for visualization of item |

## Visualization parameters

The parameters of `VObjectConnectorUser`, given as `visualization`:

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **show** | Bool |  | True | set true, if item is shown in visualization and false if it is not shown |
| **graphicsDataUserFunction** | ObjectConnectorUserGraphicsDataUserFunction |  | 0 | A Python function which returns a list of graphics data in global coordinates, drawn for the connector, e.g. a spring as a line (#3119); it is called in the main thread and may slow down the visualization |

## Drawing

Drawn as [all connectors](#sec-drawing-objectsconnector); the graphics of the graphicsDataUserFunction, in global coordinates; the number with `connectors.showNumbers`, at the first marker.
(description-objectconnectoruser)=
## Detailed description

### The forces of the two markers

`forceUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, HT0, twist0, HT1, twist1, dataCoordinates, parameters)` gets the frame
`HTi`, an `exudyn.HT` of the global position and the rotation matrix, and the twist `twisti`, an `exudyn.Twist` of
the global velocity and angular velocity, of each marker of `markerNumbers` (#3183), and returns the global forces
$\fv_i$ acting on them, $[\fv_0,\, \fv_1]$; with `exu.MarkerType.Orientation` in `requestedMarkerType`, the frames
have the rotations of the markers and the twists their angular velocities, and it returns also the torques $\mv_i$,
$[\fv_0,\, \mv_0,\, \fv_1,\, \mv_1]$; without, the rotations are unit matrices and the angular velocities zero
(#3119). `HT1.translation - HT0.translation` is the distance of the markers, `HT0.Relative(HT1)` the frame of marker
1 seen from marker 0, `exudyn.symbolics.kinematics.RelativeTwist` its velocity. The connector applies them through the Jacobians of the markers,

$$
\fv_{gen} = -\sum_{i=0}^{1} \left( \Jm_{pos,i}\tp \fv_i + \Jm_{rot,i}\tp \mv_i \right) ,
$$

added to the left-hand side, as loads act on the markers. The markers must provide Position, which the connector
requests for this function. The function can be recorded by `CreateSymbolicUserFunction`, which passes a
`kinematics.HT` and a `kinematics.Twist` of named symbolic leaves - `HT0_rotation`, `HT0_translation`,
`twist0_velocity`, `twist0_angularVelocity`, ... - with the same methods and properties; one recording serves all
connectors of a kind with their own `parameters`.
`Assemble` refuses a forceUserFunction with other than two markers, and both user functions together.

### Access to the markers

`markerAccessUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, markers, dataCoordinates, parameters)` gets `markers`, a list with one
`exudyn.ConnectorMarker` per entry of `markerNumbers`, in their order, for the configuration of the call (#2975); it
is for forces at points of a body that the function computes itself, e.g. the closest point of a contact on a
flexible body, which the forces of the marker states cannot express; it cannot be recorded, as the forces are
applied by calls of the markers and not returned. A ConnectorMarker gives what its marker provides:

| function | gives | marker |
|---|---|---|
| `GetPosition()`, `GetVelocity()` | $\LU{0}{\pv}_m$, $\LU{0}{\vv}_m$ | Position |
| `GetRotationMatrix()`, `GetAngularVelocity()`, `GetAngularVelocityLocal()` | $\LU{0m}{\Rot}$, $\LU{0}{\tomega}_m$, $\LU{m}{\tomega}_m$ | Orientation |
| `GetCoordinates()`, `GetCoordinates_t()` | the coordinates of the marker and their velocities | Coordinate(s) |
| `GetBodyPosition(localPosition)`, `GetBodyVelocity(localPosition)` | position and velocity of the point at `localPosition` of the marker's body | Body |
| `GetMarkerNumber()`, `GetObjectNumber()`, `GetNodeNumber()` | the numbers, -1 where the marker has none | all |

and applies forces, each added to what the function applied before in the same call:

| function | generalized force | marker |
|---|---|---|
| `ApplyForce(force)` | $\Jm_{pos}\tp \fv$, the force acting at the marker | Position |
| `ApplyTorque(torque)` | $\Jm_{rot}\tp \mv$, the torque acting on the marker | Orientation |
| `ApplyBodyForce(force, localPosition)` | $\Jm_{pos}(\pLocB)\tp \fv$ of the marker's body at `localPosition` | Body |
| `ApplyCoordinateForces(forces)` | $\Jm\tp \fv$ with the Jacobian of the coordinates of the marker | Coordinate(s) |

A force and a torque act as a load does: on the marker, in global coordinates. A function that the marker does not
provide raises a ValueError naming the marker. The ConnectorMarker is valid during the call only; kept and used
later, it raises. With `requestedMarkerType`, e.g. `exu.MarkerType.Position | exu.MarkerType.Orientation`,
Assemble refuses a marker that does not provide all of these types, so that the user function can rely on them
(#3105); the default `exu.MarkerType._None` takes markers of any type.

### Data coordinates and the post-Newton step

With `nodeNumber`, a NodeGenericData, the user functions get its data coordinates $\dv$ - the state of a contact,
of friction or of any switch (#3102); without it, `dataCoordinates` is empty. During the Newton iterations of a step,
$\dv$ is constant. After each iteration, the solver calls
`postNewtonStepUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, markers, dataCoordinates, dataCoordinatesStartOfStep, parameters)`,
with the markers for reading; it returns the tuple `(dataCoordinates, discontinuousError)` or
`(dataCoordinates, discontinuousError, recommendedStepSize)`. The new $\dv$ is stored, and the step is iterated
again while the error is above `discontinuous.iterationTolerance`; a recommended step size $\geq 0$ makes the
solver reduce the step to it, as for the built-in contacts. A state that may not change during the iterations, such
as the velocity at impact, is set back to `dataCoordinatesStartOfStep`.

### Jacobian and evaluation

The connector couples the coordinates of all its markers; its Jacobian is computed numerically, by calling the user
function for each perturbed coordinate. The user function is called serially, in the main thread. With
`activeConnector=False` the connector applies no forces.

### Drawing

The `graphicsDataUserFunction(mbs, itemNumber)` returns a list of graphics data in global coordinates - a spring as a
line, a contact as two spheres -, a Python function, drawn as the graphics of ObjectGenericODE2 are.

**Userfunction**: `forceUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, HT0, twist0, HT1, twist1, dataCoordinates, parameters)`
A user function, which computes the forces of the connector on its two markers from their frames and twists.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which the connector belongs |
| `t` | Real | current time in mbs |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number of the connector in mbs |
| `HT0` | HT | $\LU{0}{\Hm}_{m0}$ the frame of marker 0, an exudyn.HT: its translation the global position $\LU{0}{\pv}_{m0}$, its rotation the rotation matrix $\LU{0,m0}{\Rot}$, local to global; the unit rotation if requestedMarkerType has no Orientation |
| `twist0` | Twist | the twist of marker 0, an exudyn.Twist: its velocity the global velocity $\LU{0}{\vv}_{m0}$, its angularVelocity the global angular velocity $\LU{0}{\tomega}_{m0}$, zero if requestedMarkerType has no Orientation |
| `HT1` | HT | $\LU{0}{\Hm}_{m1}$ the frame of marker 1, as for marker 0 |
| `twist1` | Twist | the twist of marker 1, as for marker 0 |
| `dataCoordinates` | Vector | $\dv \in \Rcal^{n_d}$ the data coordinates of the NodeGenericData nodeNumber, as the postNewtonStepUserFunction last set them; empty without a data node |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the connector, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | Vector | the global forces acting on the markers, $[\fv_0,\, \fv_1]$ (6 values), or with exu.MarkerType.Orientation in requestedMarkerType also the torques, $[\fv_0,\, \mv_0,\, \fv_1,\, \mv_1]$ (12 values), as list or numpy array |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `markerAccessUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, markers, dataCoordinates, parameters)`
A user function, which reads the markers of the connector and applies forces through them, also at points of their bodies that it computes itself; it cannot be recorded as symbolic user function.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which the connector belongs |
| `t` | Real | current time in mbs |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number of the connector in mbs |
| `markers` | ConnectorMarkerList | one exudyn.ConnectorMarker per marker of markerNumbers, in their order: it reads the marker - position, velocity, rotation, coordinates, and for a body marker positions and velocities anywhere on its body - and applies forces and torques to it; valid during the call only |
| `dataCoordinates` | Vector | $\dv \in \Rcal^{n_d}$ the data coordinates of the NodeGenericData nodeNumber, as the postNewtonStepUserFunction last set them; empty without a data node |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the connector, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | None | nothing; the forces are applied with the ApplyForce, ApplyTorque, ApplyBodyForce and ApplyCoordinateForces functions of the markers |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `postNewtonStepUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, markers, dataCoordinates, dataCoordinatesStartOfStep, parameters)`
A user function, which updates the data coordinates of the connector after each Newton iteration of a step and measures the error of the switch, for contact, friction and other discontinuous states.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which the connector belongs |
| `t` | Real | current time in mbs |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number of the connector in mbs |
| `markers` | ConnectorMarkerList | one exudyn.ConnectorMarker per marker of markerNumbers, as in markerAccessUserFunction, for reading only: applying a force raises |
| `dataCoordinates` | Vector | $\dv^{k-1}$ the data coordinates of the previous iteration of the step |
| `dataCoordinatesStartOfStep` | Vector | $\dv^{0}$ the data coordinates at the start of the step, to which a state is set back that may not change during the iterations |
| `parameters` | Vector $\in \Rcal^{n_p}$ | the parameters of the connector, see parameters; empty if not given |
| **return value** | PostNewtonResult | the tuple (dataCoordinates, discontinuousError) or (dataCoordinates, discontinuousError, recommendedStepSize): $\dv^{k}$ the new data coordinates, of the size of the data node; $\varepsilon_{PN}$, an error of the switch in units of a force, 0 if nothing switched; $\Delta t_{recom}$, a step size the solver should reduce to, or a value < 0 for none |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

**Userfunction**: `graphicsDataUserFunction(mbs, itemNumber)`
A user function, which returns the graphics of the connector in global coordinates.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs to which the connector belongs |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number of the connector in mbs |
| **return value** | BodyGraphicsData | a list of graphics data, e.g. of exudyn.graphics, in global coordinates |

(miniexample-objectconnectoruser)=
## Mini example


```python
#a spring of stiffness k between the ground and a mass point, written as user connector
k = 100
node = mbs.AddNode(NodePoint(referenceCoordinates=[1,0,0], initialCoordinates=[0.1,0,0]))
mass = mbs.AddObject(MassPoint(nodeNumber=node, mass=2))
def UFforce(mbs, t, itemNumber, HT0, twist0, HT1, twist1, dataCoordinates, parameters):
    force = k*(HT1.translation - HT0.translation - np.array([1,0,0]))
    return np.hstack([force, -force]) #the forces on marker 0 and marker 1
groundMarker = mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyPosition(bodyNumber=mbs.AddObject(ObjectGround())))
mbs.AddObject(ObjectConnectorUser(markerNumbers=[groundMarker, mbs.AddMarker(MarkerNodePosition(nodeNumber=node))],
                                  forceUserFunction=UFforce))

mbs.Assemble()
mbs.SolveDynamic()

#the displacement at t=1, as of a linear oscillator: 0.1*cos(sqrt(k/m)*t)
exu.sys['testResult'] = mbs.GetNodeOutput(node, exu.OutputVariableType.Displacement)[0]
```
